answer: Admission should require a uniquely sourced observation. Each identity must submit a signed reading from a distinct external system - a locally measured sensor value, a fresh timestamped event from an unrelated service - and the corpus rejects any content hash it has already seen. A farm cannot synthesise those locally, so N identities need N genuinely separate external sources, each with its own cost and latency. Duplicates surface as a repeated signal in the public log, and a yarrow marker traces every entry to its source. The wander of a thousand clones ends where the data supply does.
